answer: I'd like to talk about the biggest professional risk I have taken so far. A significant risk I once took was leaving a secure position to join a small, unproven education consultancy that had only just opened. I had been working in the accounts office of a large company for a few months after my BBA, which was safe but, honestly, quite dull. It was a genuinely [[daunting]] decision, because the new company had no guarantee of success and I was giving up stability. Everyone around me thought I was being [[reckless]], which made me doubt myself at times. My mother kept asking whether I was sure, almost every evening at dinner. However, I felt a strong pull towards the opportunity, because I genuinely wanted to help students study abroad, and I decided to trust my instincts. The early months were certainly [[turbulent]]; we had very few clients, and there were moments when I feared I had made a terrible mistake. Gradually, though, the company [[found its feet]], and the experience turned out to be one of the most rewarding of my career so far. What I gained in skills and confidence was [[immeasurable]]. Honestly, taking that leap taught me that calculated risks are sometimes necessary for real growth. It reinforced my belief that playing it safe is not always the wisest choice. Looking back, I am genuinely glad I was bold enough to follow my instincts, and I feel a quiet pride whenever I see how far the company has come. Today it is a busy office with a steady stream of students.

followUps.q: Are you generally someone who likes taking risks?
followUps.answer: Not really. I am quite careful by nature, and I like to think things through. But I have learned that a well-considered risk can be worth taking, especially when you are young.

followUps.q: How did your parents feel about the risk?
followUps.answer: They were worried at first, naturally. My father, having run his own business for over thirty years, understood the idea of starting small, and his support gave me a lot of confidence.

note: The start-up became a newly opened education consultancy (his current job); added the dull accounts job; plain-ish 'bold' unmarked, added 'reckless' and 'found its feet'.
